answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table because compliance has ruled the security patch must not be reverted, even though memory_b1 shows rollback has historically cleared checkout error spikes cleanly. That tool is not available here. Regional failover (memory_b2) was effective for latency recovery historically, but failover under peak settlement write load risks transaction loss or double-processing — the primary objective is sustaining availability without losing customer writes, and a failover move now is high-blast-radius under heavy writes. Add capacity is too slow for a 90-minute latency climb at peak settlement; provisioning lead time won't help within this single intervention window. Enable circuit breaker (memory_b4) contains partner failure cleanly but the signal here is write-path latency under our own load, not a dependency failure — tripping breakers would drop legitimate settlement writes, directly violating the primary objective. Route read replicas (memory_b5) is the lowest-risk move that directly addresses the observed symptom: offloading read pressure from the primary has historically recovered transactional write latency the same day. At peak write load, even a small reduction in read contention on the primary can meaningfully relieve p99 latency. This preserves the security patch (no code revert), keeps write traffic flowing, and is reversible. Before full rollout I would scope it as a small guarded test — route a narrow dashboard/report cohort first, confirm write p99 responds, then widen. I want memory_b1 verified to confirm rollback's historical behavior is as remembered and that I'm not underestimating a viable revert path, and memory_b5 verified to confirm the read-replica-offload pattern genuinely recovered write latency in the prior incident, which is the lever I'm actually pulling. Other memories don't bear directly on the read-replica hypothesis or the rollback constraint already established by compliance.
